title: Flat-resolution scalar extension with the canonical comparison
statement:
Let $A\to A'$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and let $N$ be an $A$-module. Let $q:C\to N[0]$ be a quasi-isomorphism of cochain complexes of $A$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose $C^i=0$ for all $i>b$ for some integer $b$, and every $C^i$ is flat, meaning that tensoring with it preserves exact sequences. Write $T(K)=K\otimes_A A'$ for termwise scalar extension [def-weil-module-base-change] and $Q_A:K(A)\to D(A)$, $Q_{A'}:K(A')\to D(A')$ for localization; maps of complexes in these categories mean their homotopy images. There exists a universal total left derived pair $(L,\gamma)$ for $Q_{A'}T$, with $L:D(A)\to D(A')$ and natural counit $\gamma:LQ_A\to Q_{A'}T$ in the convention of [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class]. In particular the sheaf scalar-extension pair [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], transported by the exact tensor evaluation equivalence [lem-trf-one-point-derived-ring-identification], is such a pair. For every such pair, $C$ is K-flat [def-pc-module-kflat-complex], $\gamma_C$ is invertible, and
$$j_q=L(Q_Aq)\circ\gamma_C^{-1}:Q_{A'}(C\otimes_A A')\xrightarrow{\sim}L(Q_A(N[0]))$$
is an isomorphism in $D(A')$. It identifies the tensor augmentation with the canonical derived-to-ordinary counit: with $T(N[0])=(N\otimes_A A')[0]$, the equality in $D(A')$ is
$$\gamma_{N[0]}\circ j_q=Q_{A'}(q\otimes1).$$
Here $\gamma_{N[0]}$ is the counit of the supplied universal pair, not an independently chosen comparison map. No flatness of $A'$ over $A$, projectivity of the terms of $C$, or finite generation is assumed.

source.place: Tag 08QP (lemma-flat-base-change), proof, computation of derived scalar extension using the free resolution s(P); generalized here to a bounded-above flat resolution and made counit-compatible.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat] with $R=A$ and $P=C$. Its hypotheses are exactly the given upper bound and termwise tensor-flatness. Thus $C$ is K-flat in the ordinary acyclic-total-tensor sense.

On the one-object site, use [lem-trf-ringed-scalar-universal-resolution-comparison] for $\underline A\to\underline {A\prime}$ and transport its pair by [lem-trf-one-point-derived-ring-identification]. The site is small. Evaluation and its inverse preserve K-flatness, termwise scalar extension and the universal counit. We obtain a universal ordinary-module pair $(L_0,\varepsilon)$ with $\varepsilon_C$ invertible. Its functor is precisely the transported sheaf derived change of rings specified in the statement.

source.place: Tag 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change), fixed-site change of rings; derived.tex Tag 06XN (lemma-find-existence-computes), dual assertion; terminal-site specialization and counit transport.

proof.text: For any supplied universal pair $(L,\gamma)$, the universal property in [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class] gives unique $a:L\to L_0$ and $b:L_0\to L$ with $\varepsilon\circ(aQ_A)=\gamma$ and $\gamma\circ(bQ_A)=\varepsilon$. Their composites satisfy the same counit equations as the identities, so uniqueness gives $ba=1_L$ and $ab=1_{L_0}$. Hence $a$ is a natural isomorphism and $\gamma_C=\varepsilon_C\circ a_{Q_AC}$ is invertible.

source.place: Tag 06XN (lemma-find-existence-computes) and equation-everywhere; uniqueness of a universal pair, written out from its universal property.

proof.text: By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $Q_Aq$ is invertible since $q$ is a quasi-isomorphism. A functor preserves inverses: applying $L$ to the two inverse equations shows that $L(Q_Aq)$ is invertible. Therefore $j_q=L(Q_Aq)\circ\gamma_C^{-1}$ is an isomorphism with source $Q_{A\prime}T(C)$ and target $L(Q_A(N[0]))$.

source.place: Tag 08QP (lemma-flat-base-change), proof: compute derived scalar extension with a flat resolution; localization and composition of inverses.

proof.text: Naturality of the supplied $\gamma$ at $q$ says $\gamma_{N[0]}\circ L(Q_Aq)=Q_{A\prime}T(q)\circ\gamma_C$. Compose on the right with $\gamma_C^{-1}$ to obtain $\gamma_{N[0]}\circ j_q=Q_{A\prime}T(q)$. By [def-weil-module-base-change], $T(q)=q\otimes1$ on each term and $T(N[0])=(N\otimes_A A\prime)[0]$: tensoring a zero term gives zero, and the sole remaining differential is zero. This is the required equality with the very counit of the supplied pair; no exactness of $T$ on arbitrary complexes was used.

source.place: Tag 06XN (lemma-find-existence-computes), universal counit of equation-everywhere; naturality and cancellation.
